rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 (outer sensors forward to y = 0.05, inner three at y = 0.03, kd 0.5, kp 3.0, base_speed 1.4, sensor_size 0.012) is the best raced design at 173.5, up from 154.1. The oval improved (progress 0.67 to 0.74, mean finish time 1.97 s, 2 of 20 finishes against 1 of 20), and the s-bend improved (progress 0.30 to 0.32). The s-bend line-loss count rose from 1.00 to 1.15, so the forward offset did not reduce line loss, but it did not stop progress. The entityR1 feedback approved the iteration 6 geometry, but it was written against iteration 1 (154.1), so its 'keep the offset' rule is now satisfied by the score. Its line-loss condition (below 0.9 on the s-bend or slalom) is not met, so the rule is only partly applicable. Completions dominate the score (500 points each), and the oval is the only track that has finished. Oval finish time at base_speed 1.4 was about 1.97 s, close to the 3.0 s cap with margin, so speed is the main lever for completions.

Change. Keep the iteration 6 geometry and all controller gains. Raise controller.base_speed from 1.4 to 1.6, which is the single variable changed. The rationale is to raise the chance of finishing the oval and s-bend within 3.0 s. Expected result: oval finish time falls to about 1.6 s with more completions, and progress holds or rises on the s-bend and slalom. Risk: a faster robot may leave the track on bends (the off-track limit is 0.06 m), so line loss and max_error may rise. If runs go off track sooner (progress drops below about 0.3 on the s-bend, or oval progress falls below 0.70), revert to base_speed 1.4 and test ki 0.15 next to address line loss.

Hypotheses. (a) Speed 1.6 converts oval near-finishes into completions; the oval has about 0.74 progress, so a shorter time may be enough. (b) Line loss stays at about 1.0 per run because the cause is turn-in lag rather than sensing lead; ki or a line-loss behaviour change is the next lever if speed does not help.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, so that the speed effect can be separated from line loss and oscillation.
